title: Curves through prescribed points preserving a finite cover
statement:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth, geometrically connected, affine scheme of
relative dimension $d\geq2$ over a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, let
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let $T\to X$ be a
finite etale morphism with $T$ connected, and let $S\subset X(k)$ be a
nonempty finite set. There are a smooth connected affine curve $C$ over
$k$ and a closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ whose image contains
$S$, such that $T\times_X C$ is connected and $C$ is defined over a
finite extension $\mathbf F_{q^m}$, $m\ge1$: there is an automorphism
$\varphi$ of $C$ with $i\circ\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma)^m\circ i$,
where $\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma$ is the geometric Galois Frobenius
of $X$.

proof.text: Work first over the algebraically closed field $k$, without requiring a finite-field model of intermediate cuts. For any smooth connected affine $Y/k$ of pure dimension $e\ge2$, any connected finite etale cover $P\to Y$, and the prescribed set $S$, apply [lem-zl-bertini-prescribed-point-smooth-system] to choose $n,V_n,U_{\rm sm}$. The system on $Y$ satisfies all hypotheses of [lem-zl-bertini-finite-cover-irreducible-system]; let $U_{\rm irr}$ be its nonempty open. Their intersection is nonempty since $\mathbf A(V_n)$ is irreducible, and has a $k$-point since $k$ is algebraically closed. Its zero scheme $Y_1$ is closed affine, smooth of pure dimension $e-1$, contains $S$, and is geometrically irreducible. The inverse image $P_1=P\times_Y Y_1$ is connected and finite etale over $Y_1$.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 2-4, simultaneous choice of a member

proof.text: Induct on the positive dimension $e$ for the assertion that such a pair $(Y,P)$ has a closed smooth connected affine curve through $S$ with connected inverse image. If $e=1$, take $Y$ and its identity immersion. If $e\ge2$, Step 1 gives $(Y_1,P_1)$ in dimension $e-1$ with the same prescribed points; apply the induction hypothesis to it. Compose the closed immersions to obtain a closed curve in $Y$: on affine coordinate rings these are successive quotient maps, whose composite is surjective. The defining pullback squares identify its inverse image in $P$ with that in $P_1$. Starting with $(X,T)$ proves the geometric conclusion. Every use of Step 1 has $e\ge2$, including the final cut from dimension two.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, iteration to dimension one

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-bertini-finite-field-descent] to the resulting closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. The original $X_0$ is of finite type since it is smooth and affine over $k_0$. This gives $m\ge1$, the closed model $C_m$ over $\mathbf F_{q^m}$, and the automorphism $\varphi$ satisfying $i\circ\varphi=g_X^m\circ i$. With $g_X=\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma$, this is exactly the required Frobenius stability. All geometric properties are those obtained in Step 2.

source.place: Proof last paragraph, finite constant-field descent

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth, geometrically connected, affine scheme of
relative dimension $d\geq2$ over a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, let
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let $T\to X$ be a
finite etale morphism with $T$ connected, and let $S\subset X(k)$ be a
nonempty finite set. There are a smooth connected affine curve $C$ over
$k$ and a closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ whose image contains
$S$, such that $T\times_X C$ is connected and $C$ is defined over a
finite extension $\mathbf F_{q^m}$, $m\ge1$: there is an automorphism
$\varphi$ of $C$ with $i\circ\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma)^m\circ i$,
where $\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma$ is the geometric Galois Frobenius
of $X$.

proof.text:
We spell out the geometric input. We use the ordinary Bertini lemmas
[Stacks Project, Tag 0FD5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FD5)
(sections vanishing on a prescribed closed subscheme),
[Tag 0FD6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FD6)
(smoothness), and
[Tag 0G4F](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G4F)
(geometric irreducibility of a linear system).
These are statements about schemes and linear systems, with no weight
or monodromy hypothesis.

Embed $X$ in projective space and let $\overline X$ be its
projective closure. For a sufficiently large $n$, let $V$ be
the space of sections of $\mathcal O_{\overline X}(n)$ vanishing
on the reduced finite subscheme $S$. Tag 0FD5 makes its base locus
on $X$ exactly $S$, and makes its associated map an immersion on
$X\setminus S$. Increasing $n$ if necessary makes

$$
V\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{s\in S}
(\mathfrak m_s/\mathfrak m_s^2)\otimes
\mathcal O_{\overline X}(n)|_s
$$

surjective. Indeed, apply the usual eventual vanishing of coherent
$H^1$ for an ample twist to the ideal of the union of the first
infinitesimal neighborhoods of these finitely many points. Thus
nonzero first derivative at each $s$ is a nonempty open condition
on $V$. Tag 0FD6 on $X\setminus S$, together with these finitely
many derivative conditions, makes a general member smooth everywhere
on $X$.

For completeness, the hypotheses of Tag 0G4F hold both on $X$ and
for the pulled-back linear system on $T$. Both schemes are smooth
and connected over $k$, hence irreducible. The respective base
loci are $S$ and its finite inverse image, of codimension at least
two. Choose $x\in X\setminus S$. Since the linear system induces
an immersion there, choose two sections vanishing at $x$ with
independent differentials, and a third section nonzero at $x$.
The common zero locus of the first two has a codimension-two component
through $x$ not contained in the third divisor. At any point of
$T$ above $x$, etaleness gives the same assertion for the
pulled-back sections. These verify the remaining hypothesis of
Tag 0G4F. A general member therefore cuts both $X$ and $T$
in irreducible subschemes. Intersect the finitely many nonempty open
conditions on the irreducible parameter space $V$, and choose a
$k$-point in their intersection.

The resulting $X_1$ is a smooth connected closed affine subscheme
of dimension $d-1$, contains $S$, and its inverse image $T_1$
is connected and finite etale over it. Repeat this construction until
dimension one. In dimension two the same argument applies, since
the finite base locus still has codimension two. This proves the
claim about $C$. Over $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ all the finitely
many defining equations and morphisms involve only finitely many
coefficients, so descend to one finite constant-field extension.
Geometric smoothness and connectedness are the properties just proved
after base change to $k$.
